name: The Bahamas

legalStatuses.label: Sole proprietor
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual, under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person. Usually the simplest way to start.
legalStatuses.feeNote: You need a business licence from the Department of Inland Revenue. The initial filing fee is about B$100.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.feeNote: A company costs more to set up than a business name. The registry will quote you the current fees.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and register it (a company is incorporated at the Registrar General's Department)
launchSteps.plain: A sole proprietor does not need to incorporate, but must hold a business licence. A company must be incorporated first.

launchSteps.label: Get your business licence from the Department of Inland Revenue
launchSteps.plain: Anyone carrying on business in The Bahamas needs one, even when sales are too low to pay any licence tax. You renew it every year.

launchSteps.label: Register with the National Insurance Board (NIB)
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people should register within 10 working days of starting, and decide at the start of each year the income their contributions are based on.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register as an employer with NIB (form R.1) and prepare monthly payments
launchSteps.plain: With employees you pay National Insurance each month (form C-10), by the 15th of the following month.

launchSteps.label: Register for VAT
launchSteps.plain: Required when your taxable sales reach B$100,000 in twelve months.

contributions.label: National Insurance (NIB)
contributions.plain: National Insurance gives access to a pension and other benefits. Self-employed people pay 10.3% of their declared insurable income, up to B$830 a week.

vat.label: Value Added Tax
vat.registerNote: Some activities must register whatever their sales.
vat.filingNote: Returns and payment are due within 21 days after each period.

calendar.monthlyText: Self-employed: pay your National Insurance contribution. Ask NIB for your payment schedule.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: Renew your business licence and file your turnover return for the year before.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay National Insurance for the previous month (form C-10).
calendar.vatText: If registered for VAT: file your return and pay within 21 days after each period.

notes: The Bahamas has no income tax on profit. The main costs are National Insurance, VAT (above B$100,000 in sales) and the business licence tax.

The business licence tax is charged on your total yearly sales, not on your profit. Under the 2023 Business Licence Act, sales up to B$100,000 are not taxed in this estimate, then the rate for your band applies to all your sales: 0.5% up to B$500,000, 0.75% up to B$5 million and 1.25% above. An older rule charged a flat B$100 for the smallest businesses, so confirm with the Department of Inland Revenue what you owe in your first years.
